body.h4: Around 4 in 10 businesses report rise in the price of goods and services bought
body.text: Around 4 in 10 (41%) trading businesses reported a rise in the price of goods or services bought in December 2022 compared with the previous month, according to [data collected between 9 and 22 January 2023](https://www.ons.gov.uk/releases/businessinsightsandimpactontheukeconomy26january2023).

body.h4: Around 4 in 10 businesses report rise in the price of goods and services bought
body.text: Around one in six trading businesses (17%) reported an increase in the price of goods or services sold over the same period.

body.h4: Around 4 in 10 businesses report rise in the price of goods and services bought
body.text: Looking ahead to February 2023, around a quarter (26%) of trading businesses expect the price of goods and services sold to rise.

body.h4: Around 4 in 10 businesses report rise in the price of goods and services bought
body.text: Among these, energy prices remain the top reason for businesses raising their prices, with 35% reporting this as a factor. This was followed by the price of raw materials (27%) and labour costs (23%).

body.h4: Around 4 in 10 businesses report rise in the price of goods and services bought
body.text: When looking ahead to February 2023, nearly one in five (19%) businesses reported energy prices were their main concern, followed by inflation of goods and services prices (16%) and falling demand of goods and services (13%).

body.h4: Around 4 in 10 businesses report rise in the price of goods and services bought
body.text: This was according to [data collected between 23 January 2023 and 5 February 2023](https://www.ons.gov.uk/releases/businessinsightsandimpactontheukeconomy9february2023).

body.h4: Around 4 in 10 businesses report rise in the price of goods and services bought
body.text: Amid ongoing strike action, around one in six (16%) trading private sector businesses were affected as a result of industrial action in December 2022.

body.h4: Around 4 in 10 businesses report rise in the price of goods and services bought
body.text: A quarter (25%) of those businesses reported they were unable to obtain necessary goods and 21% were unable to obtain necessary services.

body.h4: Around 4 in 10 businesses report rise in the price of goods and services bought
body.text: [In December 2022](https://www.ons.gov.uk/businessindustryandtrade/business/businessservices/bulletins/businessinsightsandimpactontheukeconomy/26january2023), almost a third (30%) of trading businesses reported their turnover had fallen compared with the previous month.This was highest among businesses in the wholesale and retail trade industry, at 46%.In mid-January 2023, a quarter (25%) of businesses reported their staffing costs had risen over the previous three months, with the accommodation and food service activities industry reporting the highest proportion of businesses whose staffing costs had increased (44%).[In late December 2022](https://www.ons.gov.uk/releases/businessinsightsandimpactontheukeconomy5january2023), 5% of businesses with 10 or more employees said they expect to make redundancies over the next three months. The most commonly reported reasons for doing so were to reduce staff costs (69%) and certain job roles no longer being required (29%).

body.text: [In December 2022](https://www.ons.gov.uk/businessindustryandtrade/business/businessservices/bulletins/businessinsightsandimpactontheukeconomy/26january2023), almost a third (30%) of trading businesses reported their turnover had fallen compared with the previous month.

body.h4: Around 4 in 10 businesses report rise in the price of goods and services bought
body.text: This was highest among businesses in the wholesale and retail trade industry, at 46%.
